headers.//: Vite fingerprints every asset filename, so they can be cached forever.
The service worker itself must never be cached. A stale sw.js pins every returning visitor to whatever caching rules it shipped with, and nothing served from the site can talk them out of it.

The entry document must never be cached, or a deploy stays invisible until the old copy expires. Both sources are needed: a visit to '/' is served through the rewrite below and never matches the literal '/index.html'.
Crash Rivals is a legacy page, not a fingerprinted asset.
Character models are megabytes and worth caching, but the filenames are not fingerprinted — an hour, so dropping in a new export shows up the same day.
Fixed filenames, so an hour: long enough to be cheap, short enough that a new icon or a renamed app appears the same day.
